meta.title: Weekend Getaways from Toronto
meta.subtitle: Five trips, five directions
meta.all_prices_are_for: two people together, unless a line says per_person
notes: Trip 'kingston-pec' is flagged featured:false - superseded by Montreal, which covers the same direction. The other four are featured:true. 'muskoka' and 'algonquin-haliburton' are two ALTERNATIVE versions of the north trip - use the alternative_to field to group them in the UI rather than showing them as unrelated offerings.
Coordinates are deliberately omitted. Every place has a maps_query string instead — feed it to Google Maps, Mapbox geocoding, or an embed URL.
cost.amount of 0 means genuinely free. cost.amount of null means unknown/needs a phone call.
data_source on a stop or lodging option names where the numbers came from and when. Anything without one is still my estimate.

Budget: read budget.total for the headline number and budget.variants[] for the alternatives. A variant with total:null has total_range instead (a string like '1150-1350') - Quebec City flying and Georgian Bay with-pottery are the only two.

Every stop is guaranteed to have: time, name, type, description, duration_min, cost{amount,per,note}, maps_query, tags[], address. Any of these may be null, but the key is always present. Everything else is optional.
meta.revision_note: v2.0 - schema normalised for the build. Every trip now has the same budget shape (total + variants[]), and every stop has the same required keys. Content unchanged from v1.2.

trips.name: Muskoka
trips.tagline: Lakes, pioneer history and a steam train
trips.summary: The original plan. Bracebridge as a base, Huntsville and Arrowhead to the north on Saturday, Gravenhurst and a pottery workshop on the way home Sunday. Cottage country in fall colour.
trips.why_this_trip: Closest of the three. Strongest nature-to-effort ratio, a confirmed pottery booking, and the only one with a genuine cottage-country feel.

dates.label: Thanksgiving weekend
why: Fall colour in central Ontario peaks around Thanksgiving weekend - Ontario Parks' own guidance.
Muskoka Heritage Place closes for the season Oct 10, and the Portage Flyer steam train runs Tue-Sat only. Saturday Oct 10 is the LAST possible day to do the train and pioneer village this year.
Lodging is cheaper this weekend than the previous one - checked, and it is not close.
dates.note: Monday Oct 12 is the Thanksgiving holiday, so a third day is available if you want it.

lodging.surprise: Thanksgiving weekend is CHEAPER here than the weekend before. Oct 2-4 came back at $448-$576 for the same places. Counterintuitive, but that is what the live rates say - and it is another reason to take the Oct 9-11 dates.
lodging.caveat: This is the most expensive lodging of the three trips. Muskoka in peak colour is simply pricey.

trips.name: Algonquin & Haliburton Highlands
trips.tagline: The famous one — maple hills, logging history and a sculpture forest
trips.summary: The other way to do the north. Nothing here overlaps with the Muskoka plan — you drive past Bracebridge and keep going. Saturday is the Highway 60 corridor through Algonquin; Sunday comes home through Dorset and Haliburton.
trips.why_this_trip: Muskoka is lakes and towns. This is forest and art. Algonquin is the most famous park in Ontario and the best fall colour in the province, and the Haliburton side adds outdoor sculpture and a five-star pottery studio that Muskoka does not have.
how_it_differs_from_muskoka: Different base town - Huntsville, not Bracebridge
Canadian landscape art at the Algonquin Art Centre and Tom Thomson's legacy path, instead of the Group of Seven murals
Logging history instead of pioneer village history
Dorset Lookout Tower - it was only a footnote alternative in the Muskoka plan, here it is a main stop
Haliburton Sculpture Forest and Blackbird Pottery, both outside the Muskoka triangle entirely

dates.label: First full October weekend
why: Algonquin's own records put the AVERAGE sugar maple peak in the west Highway 60 corridor at September 27 - earlier than Muskoka, because it is higher and further north.
Oct 2-4 lands in what the park calls the 'Golden Encore': poplar and birch yellows plus the orange sugar maple understory. Slightly past red maple peak, still spectacular, and the crowd has thinned.
Everything is open - the Art Centre runs to about Oct 19, the Logging Museum to mid-October.
dates.warning: Algonquin's report names Sept 19/20, 26/27, Oct 3/4 and Thanksgiving as the busiest weekends of the year. Start early and expect company at the trailheads.

trips.name: Montreal
trips.tagline: A city weekend that feels like abroad
trips.summary: 542 km each way. Friday-night departure, a full Saturday of markets, old stone streets and the mountain, then a Sunday pottery class before the long drive home.
trips.why_this_trip: The only plan that scores on every single interest at once: 17th to 19th century architecture, a confirmed beginner pottery class, a real Koreatown, a manga cafe, and the most photographed church interior in the country.

trips.name: Quebec City
trips.tagline: A walled 17th-century city, and a waterfall taller than Niagara
trips.summary: The only walled city north of Mexico, a UNESCO World Heritage site you can walk end to end, and Montmorency Falls 12 km out - 83 m, thirty metres taller than Niagara.
trips.why_this_trip: Everything on her list at maximum strength: authentic architecture that is actually four centuries old, authentic food, a famous landmark, photographs everywhere you point the camera, a Korean street-food counter inside the old town, and four operational pottery studios.

the_honest_problem.headline: This is the one trip where driving stops making sense.
the_honest_problem.detail: Quebec City is 800 km from Toronto - 8 to 9 hours of driving each way, so about 17 hours in the car for a two-day trip. Every other plan here absorbs the drive. This one does not.

options.verdict: Doable with a Friday-night departure, but you will spend more time driving than in Quebec City.

options.duration: 3-4 hr door to door, usually via Montreal
options.cost_note: $150-260 one-way per person, plus $30-40 per checked bag
options.verdict: RECOMMENDED. Costs roughly the same as driving once you drop the rental, and hands you back fourteen hours. Old Quebec is walkable and Montmorency is reachable by city bus, so you do not need a car there at all.
Arrives at Gare du Palais right beside the old town, but the total time is worse than driving.

the_honest_problem.recommendation: Fly, and skip the rental entirely. If you drive, treat it as three days, not two.

dates.label: Mid-October
why: Colour on Ile d'Orleans and around Montmorency peaks early-to-mid October.
Late enough that the summer crowds in Petit-Champlain have thinned, early enough that everything is still running normal hours.
dates.collision: This clashes with the Georgian Bay trip (Oct 17-18). Pick one, or move Georgian Bay to Oct 30-31 - Scenic Caves and Old Baldy both run through October, though colour will be past peak by then.

stats.shape: Two nights minimum. Friday night out, Sunday back.

stops.transit: 12 km northeast of Old Quebec. Reachable by city bus if you have not got a car.
stops.maps_query: Parc de la Chute-Montmorency, Quebec QC

stops.name: Ile d'Orleans
stops.description: Cross the bridge just past the falls onto a farming island where some houses date to the 1600s. Cider houses, chocolatiers, bakeries, a single road around the edge with the river on one side.
stops.note: Needs a car, or take the combined falls + island tour (~$60 per person) if you flew and did not rent.

stops.name: Travel home
stops.description: Flight out, or the long drive.
stops.maps_query: Quebec City, QC to Toronto, ON

bookings.name: Flights YYZ to YQB
bookings.note: Book early. Porter flies the route; most itineraries connect through Montreal. This decides the whole budget.

bookings.name: Accommodation
bookings.note: Auberge St-Louis, 48 rue St-Louis, if you want to be inside the walls.

bookings.name: Pottery studio
bookings.note: Ceramic Cafe Studio Quebec (435 Rue Saint-Joseph E) is the most walk-in friendly; Rang Nord is the highest rated. Call either.

bookings.name: Montmorency cable car
bookings.note: Buy at the park or online. Not usually necessary to pre-book off-season.

warnings: 800 km each way. Do not attempt this as a Saturday-Sunday drive.
If you fly, you will not have a car for Ile d'Orleans - either rent at YQB for one day or take the combined falls-and-island tour.
Quebec City is overwhelmingly French-speaking. English is understood in tourist areas but far less than Montreal. Neither of you speaks French - worth knowing, not a reason to skip it.
Flight costs here are a range, not a quote. They swing the total by several hundred dollars.

alternatives.name: Add it to the Montreal trip
alternatives.note: Montreal and Quebec City are 3 hours apart. As a single 4-day trip this is far more efficient than two separate journeys east - but it breaks the two-day rule.

trips.name: Beaver Valley & Georgian Bay
trips.tagline: Cliff lookouts, waterfalls and a suspension bridge
trips.summary: Collingwood is two hours out. Escarpment lookouts over a valley, waterfalls, apple orchards, a working harbour town, and Ontario's longest suspension footbridge. Almost none of it costs money.
trips.why_this_trip: The best fall-colour drive in southern Ontario, and the one that matches the original 'forget about work' brief. Cheapest of the three to run.

alternatives.name: Scandinave Spa Blue Mountain
alternatives.description: Outdoor Nordic baths, hot pools, cold plunges, eucalyptus steam room, in the forest. Replaces everything else on Sunday.

cost.note: $135 per person Sunday, $159 Saturday in high season Sep 4 - Dec 17, taxes extra. Wednesday is $95.

praise: Immaculate grounds, hammocks, fire pits, forest lounges
Thermal circuit of hot pools, cold plunges and steam room

trips.name: Kingston & Prince Edward County
trips.tagline: Limestone city and a lake on a hill
trips.superseded_note: Covers the same direction as Montreal at a third of the distance. Kept as the budget option for the east — it fits under $500 all-in, which Montreal does not.
trips.summary: Kingston is Canada's first capital, built almost entirely of grey limestone. Day two loops home through Prince Edward County on a free cable ferry.
highlights: Springer Market Square — Ontario's oldest continuously operating farmers' market, since 1801

open_questions: Trip dates. Grey County fall colour peaks early to mid October; Muskoka peaks around Thanksgiving Oct 10-12; Montreal is better later in October.
Montreal: Friday night departure or not. It decides whether the trip is $620 or $1,000.
Collingwood pottery: needs a phone call, the only unverified anchor in the Georgian Bay plan.
Studio Mie Kim: how they handle the 5-6 week pickup for out-of-town students.

date_plan.constraint: Everything inside October 2026, nothing past Oct 31.

one_weekend_each.2026-10-02 to 04: Algonquin & Haliburton - golden encore in the Hwy 60 corridor
one_weekend_each.2026-10-09 to 11: Muskoka - Thanksgiving peak, and the last weekend for the Portage Flyer
one_weekend_each.2026-10-16 to 18: Quebec City - needs two nights, colour on Ile d'Orleans
one_weekend_each.2026-10-30 to 31: Georgian Bay - if you want all five. Past peak colour, but Scenic Caves and Old Baldy still run.

date_plan.collision: Georgian Bay's own best date is Oct 17-18, which Quebec City wants. If you are only doing some of these, give Georgian Bay Oct 17-18 and drop Quebec or push it to a longer trip.
date_plan.logic: Colour peaks north-first and inland-first. Algonquin earliest (avg sugar maple peak Sept 27), then Muskoka, then Grey County, then the cities.
hard_deadlines: Algonquin Art Centre closes about Oct 19
Muskoka Heritage Place closes Oct 10 (Portage Flyer runs Tue-Sat)
Laura Secord Homestead season ends end of October
